section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World
Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can explain how the net force affects the object’s motion and critique an incorrect force explanation and revise it using physics vocabulary.
items.evidence_job: Navigate a connected real-world force-model stimulus by identifying the system, checking a proposed model against evidence, and planning a corrected explanation of motion.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text:
A grocery cart is observed speeding up to the right. A student proposes this force model:

          120 N support ↑
  45 N ←    [cart]    → 45 N
          120 N weight ↓

(a) Identify the system represented by the diagram.
(b) What net force does the proposed model predict?
(c) Compare that prediction with the observation that the cart is speeding up to the right. Is the model consistent with the evidence?
(d) Revise one horizontal force so the model is consistent with the observation, and explain the revised motion using net force vocabulary.
items.student_html:
A grocery cart is observed speeding up to the right. A student proposes this force model:

120 N support ↑
45 N ← [cart] → 45 N
120 N weight ↓

(a) Identify the system represented by the diagram.
(b) What net force does the proposed model predict?
(c) Compare that prediction with the observation that the cart is speeding up to the right. Is the model consistent with the evidence?
(d) Revise one horizontal force so the model is consistent with the observation, and explain the revised motion using net force vocabulary.
items.answer: (a) The grocery cart. (b) 0 N net force. (c) No. A zero net force predicts unchanged velocity, not speeding up. (d) For example, change the rightward force to 60 N while keeping 45 N left; the net force is 15 N right, so the cart’s velocity changes to the right.
items.solution_text: The original model is balanced, which conflicts with the observed change in velocity. A corrected model must have a rightward net force. One valid revision is 60 N right and 45 N left, producing 15 N right.
items.solution_html: The original model is balanced, which conflicts with the observed change in velocity. A corrected model must have a rightward net force. One valid revision is 60 N right and 45 N left, producing 15 N right.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can draw a force diagram for an object in a real-world situation.
items.evidence_job: Isolate one object in a real-world system and construct a force diagram containing only interactions that act on that object.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: A person pushes a wheeled cart to the right across a level floor while it speeds up. Draw a force diagram for the cart only. Include weight, support, push, and rolling resistance with relative horizontal arrow lengths consistent with the motion change.
items.student_html: A person pushes a wheeled cart to the right across a level floor while it speeds up. Draw a force diagram for the cart only. Include weight, support, push, and rolling resistance with relative horizontal arrow lengths consistent with the motion change.
items.answer: Draw weight down and support up; draw push right longer than rolling resistance left.
items.solution_text: Only forces acting on the cart belong in its force diagram. Because it speeds up right, the horizontal net force must point right, so the rightward push arrow must exceed the resistance arrow.
items.solution_html: Only forces acting on the cart belong in its force diagram. Because it speeds up right, the horizontal net force must point right, so the rightward push arrow must exceed the resistance arrow.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can draw a force diagram for an object in a real-world situation.
items.evidence_job: Isolate one object in a real-world system and construct a force diagram containing only interactions that act on that object.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: A suitcase is pulled left across level carpet and is slowing while still moving left. Draw a force diagram for the suitcase only with vertical forces and horizontal pull/friction arrows consistent with the motion change.
items.student_html: A suitcase is pulled left across level carpet and is slowing while still moving left. Draw a force diagram for the suitcase only with vertical forces and horizontal pull/friction arrows consistent with the motion change.
items.answer: Draw weight down and support up; friction/rightward resistance must exceed the leftward pull so the net force is right.
items.solution_text: Slowing while moving left means the velocity is changing rightward. Therefore the net horizontal force is rightward.
items.solution_html: Slowing while moving left means the velocity is changing rightward. Therefore the net horizontal force is rightward.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can decide whether the forces are balanced or unbalanced.
items.evidence_job: Use a force model to decide whether forces are balanced or unbalanced and identify the representation evidence that establishes the classification.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: Force model A: 40 N ← [cart] → 40 N. Force model B: 25 N ← [cart] → 55 N. Classify each as balanced or unbalanced and cite the diagram evidence.
items.student_html: Force model A: 40 N ← [cart] → 40 N. Force model B: 25 N ← [cart] → 55 N. Classify each as balanced or unbalanced and cite the diagram evidence.
items.answer: A is balanced; B is unbalanced with 30 N net force right.
items.solution_text: Model A has equal opposite horizontal forces. Model B has a larger rightward force, leaving 30 N right.
items.solution_html: Model A has equal opposite horizontal forces. Model B has a larger rightward force, leaving 30 N right.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can decide whether the forces are balanced or unbalanced.
items.evidence_job: Use a force model to decide whether forces are balanced or unbalanced and identify the representation evidence that establishes the classification.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: A hanging decoration has 18 N upward tension and 18 N weight. A second model shows 18 N upward and 23 N downward. Classify both models.
items.student_html: A hanging decoration has 18 N upward tension and 18 N weight. A second model shows 18 N upward and 23 N downward. Classify both models.
items.answer: The first is balanced; the second is unbalanced with 5 N downward net force.
items.solution_text: Equal opposite vertical forces balance. Unequal forces leave a resultant in the direction of the larger force.
items.solution_html: Equal opposite vertical forces balance. Unequal forces leave a resultant in the direction of the larger force.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can explain how the net force affects the object’s motion and critique an incorrect force explanation and revise it using physics vocabulary.
items.evidence_job: Critique a plausible incorrect force explanation and revise the reasoning using net force, motion, and precise physics vocabulary.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: A student says, ‘The cart is moving right, so the rightward force must be larger than the leftward force.’ The cart is actually moving right at constant speed. Critique and revise the explanation.
items.student_html: A student says, ‘The cart is moving right, so the rightward force must be larger than the leftward force.’ The cart is actually moving right at constant speed. Critique and revise the explanation.
items.answer: The claim is incorrect; constant straight-line velocity means zero net force, so horizontal forces can be balanced even while the cart moves right.
items.solution_text: Motion direction and net-force direction are not the same idea. Net force determines change in velocity. Constant velocity requires no net force.
items.solution_html: Motion direction and net-force direction are not the same idea. Net force determines change in velocity. Constant velocity requires no net force.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain how the net force affects the object’s motion and critique an incorrect force explanation and revise it using physics vocabulary.

items.student_text: A student says, ‘The soccer ball is at rest, so gravity has stopped acting on it.’ The ball is resting on the ground. Correct the explanation using force vocabulary.
items.student_html: A student says, ‘The soccer ball is at rest, so gravity has stopped acting on it.’ The ball is resting on the ground. Correct the explanation using force vocabulary.
items.answer: Gravity still acts downward; the ground exerts an upward support force, and the forces balance to zero net force.
items.solution_text: Rest does not make interactions disappear. The support force and weight are both real and can cancel.
items.solution_html: Rest does not make interactions disappear. The support force and weight are both real and can cancel.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain how the net force affects the object’s motion and critique an incorrect force explanation and revise it using physics vocabulary.
items.evidence_job: Reconcile a real-world force diagram with observed motion evidence and identify which element must change when the model is inconsistent.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: Observed motion: a cart moves right at constant speed. Candidate model: 20 N ← [cart] → 35 N. Is the model consistent? If not, identify one model change that would make it consistent.
items.student_html: Observed motion: a cart moves right at constant speed. Candidate model: 20 N ← [cart] → 35 N. Is the model consistent? If not, identify one model change that would make it consistent.
items.answer: No; the model gives 15 N net force right. Make the rightward force 20 N (or otherwise balance the horizontal totals).
items.solution_text: Constant velocity requires zero net force. The candidate diagram is unbalanced, so at least one horizontal force magnitude must change until left and right totals match.
items.solution_html: Constant velocity requires zero net force. The candidate diagram is unbalanced, so at least one horizontal force magnitude must change until left and right totals match.

items.student_text: Observed motion: a sled is accelerating left. Candidate model: 50 N ← [sled] → 50 N. Is the model consistent? Revise one force to make it consistent.
items.student_html: Observed motion: a sled is accelerating left. Candidate model: 50 N ← [sled] → 50 N. Is the model consistent? Revise one force to make it consistent.
items.answer: No; the model is balanced. For example, increase the leftward force to 65 N, giving 15 N net force left.
items.solution_text: A changing velocity to the left requires a leftward net force. Equal arrows cannot represent that observation.
items.solution_html: A changing velocity to the left requires a leftward net force. Equal arrows cannot represent that observation.
